t_row_all: Show the log of every app
t_empty: No app of your fortress reports a status yet.
t_engine: The TollRoll service does not answer. Reinstalling the plugin starts it again.
e_engine: the TollRoll service does not answer
s_notify_hint: While a channel is on, TollRoll checks your apps once a minute. It tells you when an app stops answering, when it answers again and when it shows something new that needs you. Each of these is sent once.
s_n_apprise_hint: The address of a key on your Apprise API server, such as http://192.168.1.10:8000/notify/tollroll.
s_n_err_invalid: a field is missing or not valid
n_down_body: TollRoll could not read {name} for a few minutes. The TollRoll settings show why.
n_test_body: If you read this, TollRoll can reach you here.
t_quiet_hint: Reports no status, so it has no row in the tile
t_on_demand_hint: Is in the fortress only while it runs, such as during a check, and away the rest of the time
t_map_hint: Click an app to see its log.
t_alone: No other device has joined the fortress yet.
t_join_title: Join with the phrase of your fortress
t_join_text: Then every app of your fortress shows up here, with its state and its log.
t_removed_title: TollRoll was removed from the fortress
t_removed_text: Another member took TollRoll out. Enter the current phrase to come back in.
s_live: Every change is saved right away.
s_n_apprise_bad: This is not a web address. It is saved as soon as it starts with http:// or https://.
s_rejoin_hint: If one of your apps changed the phrase, enter the new one here. Until you do, TollRoll can't read the apps of the fortress.
s_help_body: Problems, wishes or suggestions? You're welcome to open an issue on GitHub, or come say hi on Discord.
s_about_body: TollRoll is a free plugin for Unraid's dashboard, built by one knight on evenings and weekends, with no accounts, no telemetry and no ads.
s_about_coin: If it has earned a place on your server, toss a coin to your knight: it helps cover the costs and keeps the project alive.
t_win_quiet: Nothing needs you and nothing is running right now.
t_win_where: Its settings are in Unraid on {devices}.
r_told_down: Let you know that {name} is not reachable
r_told_back: Let you know that {name} is reachable again
r_told_need: Let you know that {name} needs you
r_removed: Took {app} on {device} out of the fortress
h_s_md_read: {disk} had a read error. Unraid takes the data from parity where it can. Check its cable and SMART report.
h_s_md_write: {disk} had a write error. Unraid may disable the disk, so take a look at the Main page.
h_s_io: Drive {dev} reported an I/O error. Check its cable and SMART report.
h_s_link_reset: The connection to the drive on {port} was reset. A loose cable or a weak power supply is the usual cause.
h_s_smart: A drive reports worse SMART values. Its SMART report on the Main page shows the details.
h_s_unclean: Unraid was not shut down cleanly last time.
h_s_parity_schedule: A parity check started on its schedule.
h_s_parity_hand: A parity check was started by hand or by a script.
h_s_parity_unclean: A parity check started because Unraid was not shut down cleanly.
h_s_parity_resume: The paused parity check is running again.
h_s_parity_err: The parity check found a spot where parity did not match. After an unclean shutdown that is common.
h_s_mover_start: The mover started moving files between the cache and the array.
h_s_link_down: Network port {port} lost its connection. Check the cable and the switch.
h_s_web_ok: {user} signed in to the web UI from {addr}.
h_s_web_fail: A sign-in to the web UI as {user} from {addr} failed.
h_s_ssh_fail: A sign-in over SSH as {user} from {addr} failed.
h_s_oom: The server ran out of memory and stopped {proc} to free some.
h_s_oom_cg: {proc} went over its memory limit and was stopped.
h_s_fs: The file system on {disk} reports damage. Run a file system check on it soon.
h_s_fs_off: The file system on {disk} shut down after an error. Its files stay out of reach until you check it.
h_w_new_web: {user} signed in to the web UI from {addr}, an address TollRoll has not seen before.
h_w_new_ssh: {user} signed in over SSH from {addr}, an address TollRoll has not seen before.
h_w_flash: Settings on the flash drive changed: {files}.
h_w_cron: A new scheduled task was added: {task}.
h_w_guest: The share {share} is now open to guests over {proto}.
h_w_deleted: Files deleted on {disk} within a few minutes: about {n}.
h_room: /var/log is {pct}% full. The biggest file is {file} ({size}).
h_room_who: /var/log is {pct}% full. The biggest file is {file} ({size}), written by {who}.
h_room_body: /var/log is {pct}% full and {file} is the biggest file. Once it is full, Unraid can't write its logs anymore.
h_r_fail: A sign-in to {router} as {user} from {addr} failed.
h_r_new_login: {user} signed in to {router} from {addr}, an address TollRoll has not seen before.
h_r_fails: Failed sign-ins to {router} from {addr}: {n} within 10 minutes.
h_r_ids: {router} saw an intrusion attempt from {src} to {dst}: {sig}
h_r_new_device: A new device joined your network: {device} got the address {ip}.
h_r_silent: {router} has sent no log line for {h} hours.
s_router_hint: Send your router's log to this server and TollRoll watches it as well: new sign-ins to the router, changed port forwards and firewall rules, intrusion warnings, new devices on your network and a log that goes quiet. In Unraid, open Settings → Syslog Server, switch on the local syslog server and pick a folder on a pool for its files. Then set this server's address as the remote syslog server in your router, port 514 over UDP. TollRoll only reads those lines and never connects to the router.
s_router_off: Unraid's syslog server is off, so no router can send its log here yet.
s_router_wait: Unraid's syslog server is on. No router has sent its log yet.
n_digest_none: No app had anything to tell today.
s_quiet_hint: During these hours only alerts go out. Everything else waits and arrives as one message when the quiet hours end.
s_digest_hint: One message a day with what each app told you and what is still open. It also brings along whatever waited.
s_takeover: Take over the notifications of your apps
s_takeover_hint: Apps of your fortress that know TollRoll then hand their notifications to it instead of sending them on their own, so the quiet hours, the summary and the limits below apply to all of them. With this off, or while TollRoll is away, every app keeps notifying on its own.
s_flood: The same message goes out once, until it is resolved or 20 hours have passed. Each app sends at most 6 messages an hour, and all of them together 20. Anything past that waits for the next free slot.
s_levels_hint: Pick the level from which each app may notify you. Alerts always go out at once, and everything else still shows up in the daily summary.
s_levels_none: No app of your fortress has reported in yet.
a_hint: TollRoll looked at this server and found things an app of the fortress could take care of.
a_none: Nothing to suggest. Your server is in good hands.
a_backup: Nothing backs up this server yet. BombVault takes care of your backups.
a_updates: Containers run here, and nothing tells you about their updates. ShipLog shows which container has an update and what changed.
a_health: Nothing checks the health of this server. FireSquire keeps an eye on it and tells you when a restart is safe.
t_open_none: Nothing is open. Every app is doing fine.
